jobs.occupation: Chartering Broker (f/m/d) – Regional Trade & Project Cargo (Intra-Europe) (Schifffahrtskaufmann/-frau - Trampfahrt)
jobs.description:
Key Responsibilities 

Briese Chartering is an established Shipowner/Carrier based in Leer/Germany managing a modern and versatile fleet of short-sea and multipurpose (MPP) vessels ranging from 3,000 to 10,000 DWT with a strong focus on carriage of project cargo. For further information see: www.briese-chartering.com (http://www.briese-chartering.com/)   

We are seeking an experienced Chartering Broker to join our Intra-Europe Regional Trade desk. In this role you will hold commercial responsibility for maximizing the utilization and profitability of our owned and controlled tonnage. You will optimize vessel loops across Europe, securing high-yielding regional breakbulk and specialized project cargo stems by maintaining direct relationships with industrial charterers, shippers and project forwarders.

Negotiate charter parties directly with cargo owners and competitive brokers, protecting the company's commercial interests. 

Fleet Optimization & Chartering 

Fix our 3,000–10,000 DWT fleet on Voyage Charters and Contracts of Affreightment (COAs) across European trade routes (Baltic, North Sea, Continent, Mediterranean/Black Sea and North/West Africa). 

Optimize vessel routing and scheduling to minimize ballast days and maximize daily time charter equivalent returns.

Project Cargo & Voyage Estimation 

Evaluate and price specialized project cargo inquiries tailored to our vessels' capabilities. 

Perform precise voyage calculations including bunker tracking, port/terminal expenses, and laytime analysis to ensure optimal margins. 

Market Integration & Collaboration 

Leverage the north/central European shipping community while managing an active network of international chartering contacts. 

Work closely with our in-house operations and technical management teams in Leer to guarantee smooth post-fixture execution. 

Qualifications & Experience 

 Essential Criteria 

- Minimum 3 years of commercial experience on the owner’s side or with an exclusive broker specifically within the European short-sea or small-MPP sectors. 
- Solid understanding of 3k–10k DWT vessel capabilities including stowage configurations, deck strength and regional port/canal restrictions. 
- Deep knowledge of European trades including seasonal weather factors, ice clauses and short-sea port operations. 
- Fluency in English is required; proficiency in German is highly preferred given our regional hub and team integration. 

Core Skills 

- Commercial drive with a clear focus on asset P&L and strategic fleet positioning. 
- Proficiency in voyage estimation and other standard software tools (MS Office, Sedna, Netpas, etc.). 
- Existing network of direct project cargo clients, industrial shippers and European forwarders.

Anforderungen an den Bewerber: 
Erweiterte Kenntnisse: Schifffahrtsrecht, Verhandlungsführung, Wirtschaftlichkeitsberechnung
Expertenkenntnisse: Befrachtung

jobs.occupation: Master Thesis Student in the field of Aerospace Engineering (d/f/m) (Ingenieur/in - Luft- und Raumfahrttechnik)
jobs.description:
About us

Airbus pioneers sustainable aerospace for a safe and united world. The Company constantly innovates to provide efficient and technologically-advanced solutions in aerospace, defence, and connected services. In commercial aircraft, Airbus offers modern and fuel-efficient airliners and associated services. Airbus is also a European leader in defence and security and one of the world's leading space businesses. In helicopters, Airbus provides the most efficient civil and military rotorcraft solutions and services worldwide.
Job description

In order to support Airframe Architecture Department, Airbus Operations is looking for a

Master Thesis Student in the field of Aerospace Engineering (d/f/m), title of thesis: “Preliminary Structure Design of an Amphibious Firefighter Aircraft”

You are looking for a master thesis and want to get to know the work of Airbus? Then apply now! We look forward to you supporting us in the Airframe Architecture Department as a Master Thesis Student (d/f/m)!

- Location: Hamburg
- Start: 01.12.2026
- Duration: 6 months

Your location

You will be working at the largest production site for civil aircraft situated in Hamburg. Its location on the southern banks of the river Elbe includes the option to commute by ferry. Experience the special flair of Hamburg in your spare time where vibrant cosmopolitan culture meets nautic legacy.

Your benefits

- Work-life balance with a 35-hour week (flexitime).
- Mobile working after agreement with the department.
- International environment with the opportunity to network globally.
- Work with modern/diversified technologies.
- At Airbus, we see you as a valuable team member and you are not hired to brew coffee, instead you are in close contact with the interfaces and are part of our weekly team meetings.
- Opportunity to participate in the Generation Airbus Community to expand your own network.
- You will have an experienced tutor to support you.
- Traveling overseas or within Germany is possible after consultation and agreement from the department.

Your tasks and responsibilities

- Develop the preliminary structure design of a new generation amphibious firefighter aircraft focusing on the wing to fuselage attachment.
- Investigate the panorama of existing similar aircraft to understand the different technical solutions in order to define the best structural design principles
- Perform trade offs among different structural solutions applying a Design to Value approach
- You will create an Airframe Architecture Dossier, a document showing the selection of design solutions and their rationale
- You will focus on the Structural Architecture selecting the best concept for your component
- You will focus on the airframe and you will define its architectural principles
- You will minimize cost and weight, maximise manufacturability ensuring that the aircraft can be repaired quickly.
- You will develop 3D CATIA models of the Aircraft and preliminary sizing of some relevant joints.

Desired skills and qualifications

- Enrolled full-time student (d/f/m) in the area of Aerospace Engineering with focus on Aeronautical Structures (light weight) - up to five years engineering course (end of Master study)
- Fluent in English is a must, German and French is a plus
- You are able to use CATIA 5 (nice to have)
- Ability to perform preliminary sizing of loaded structures (nice to have)
- You have good skills to use OFFICE tools (Word, Excel, Powerpoint) or Google based Tools (Docs, Sheets, Slides)
- You are a team player and a motivated master student to collaborate with

Please upload the following documents: cover letter, CV, relevant transcripts, enrollment certificate.

Not a 100% match? No worries! Airbus supports your personal growth.

Take your career to a new level and apply online (https://www.airbus.com/en/careers) now!

This job requires an awareness of any potential compliance risks and a commitment to act with integrity, as the foundation for the Company’s success, reputation and sustainable growth

By submitting your CV or application you are consenting to Airbus using and storing information about you for monitoring purposes relating to your application or future employment. This information will only be used by Airbus.
Airbus is committed to achieving workforce diversity and creating an inclusive working environment. We welcome all applications irrespective of social and cultural background, age, gender, disability, sexual orientation or religious belief.

At Airbus, we support you to work, connect and collaborate more easily and flexibly. Wherever possible, we foster flexible working arrangements to stimulate innovative thinking.

As Head of HR Global Healthcare Operations, you will be the global strategic HR leader for an organization of approximately 7,500 employees across 20 sites, serving more than 100 million patients every day. - Lead and develop a team of Global HR Business Partners and leverage people analytics to anticipate workforce needs, risks, and business impact.

- Master’s degree in Human Resources, Business, or a related field, with at least 10 years of progressive global HR leadership experience in regulated Pharma, Biotech, MedTech, or operations environments.
- Proven experience partnering with Manufacturing, Quality, Regulatory, Engineering, Supply Chain, or Operations leaders in complex global organizations.
- Strong track record in workforce transformation, organization design, talent management, succession planning, leadership development, and large-scale change.
- Practical understanding of GMP/GxP expectations and their implications for workforce practices, training, leadership accountability, and inspection readiness.
- Strong executive influencing, consulting, communication, and people analytics skills; fluent English required, additional languages such as German are an advantage.

Location:  Germany

jobs.occupation: Global Head of Facilities Management (Fachwirt/in - Facility-Management)
jobs.description:
Work Your Magic with us!

Ready to explore, break barriers, and discover more? We know you’ve got big plans – so do we! Our colleagues across the globe love innovating with science and technology to enrich people’s lives with our solutions in Healthcare, Life Science, and Electronics. Together, we dream big and are passionate about caring for our rich mix of people, customers, patients, and planet. That's why we are always looking for curious minds that see themselves imagining the unimaginable with us.

One of the most operationally significant roles in the new CREM structure, the Global Head of Facilities Management is responsible for leading and transforming Merck's facilities and workplace management function across a global portfolio of 340+ locations and 4.3 million m² — encompassing offices, standalone labs, warehouses and selected soft services at manufacturing sites across more than 60 countries.
This is a dual-focus role requiring transformational vision and strict operational leadership. You will consolidate our existing FM foundation into a high-performing, data-informed ecosystem designed to minimise operational vulnerability. Through uniform service delivery standards and a consolidated regional IFM vendor model, you will drive process efficiency, strengthen risk controls, and unlock strategic business value across Merck's global footprint.
The scale of the people dimension alone is significant: this role leads a global FM organisation with a substantial team within CREM, with additional headcount transferring from business sectors as the expanded remit is stood up.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

- FM Strategy & Vision: Define and own the global FM strategy for CREM — establishing a unified vision, service delivery model and operating standards across all asset classes and geographies, aligned to Merck's broader corporate objectives.
- Transformation Leadership: Lead the FM transformation programme — driving vendor consolidation toward a consolidated regional IFM model, standing up site-level governance, managing the lift-and-shift of FM services from business sectors, and embedding a performance management culture across the function.
- Stakeholder Engagement: Build trusted relationships with business sector leads, site managers and senior Merck stakeholders — positioning FM as a value-creating partner and ensuring the function is responsive to business needs.
- Operational Leadership: Ensure consistent, high-quality FM service delivery and drive operational excellence across the full portfolio by standardising service delivery and optimising facilities performance — maintaining service continuity throughout the transformation and holding Regional Heads accountable for operational performance within their geographies.
- IFM Partner Management: Own Merck's most senior relationships with global and regional IFM providers — acting as the primary Merck counterpart in strategic vendor negotiations, performance reviews and vendor [AB8.1]management at a global level.
- FM Budget Responsibility: Manage the global FM budget, allocating, monitoring, and optimising operational and capital expenditure (OpEx/CapEx) across the portfolio to ensure cost-efficiency, regulatory compliance, and alignment with corporate financial objectives.
- Budget Authority: Hold direct budget authority for FM vendor contracts and operational spend across the full scope — managing significant global FM expenditure, driving cost efficiency and ensuring financial transparency across the function.
- Standards & Compliance: Establish and enforce binding global FM standards — covering vendor protocols, preventative maintenance schedules, H&S compliance, SLAs and performance penalties. Ensure consistent application across all geographies.
- Manufacturing FM: Oversee the delivery of selected soft FM services at manufacturing sites — working in close collaboration with the Quality & Compliance Lead to ensure service delivery meets the specific operational and regulatory requirements of Merck's manufacturing environments.
- Performance Management: Establish and own the FM KPI framework — tracking performance against industry benchmarks (IFMA, RICS), driving continuous improvement and ensuring data-driven decision making is embedded across the function to achieve operational excellence.
- People Management: Lead, develop and inspire a global FM organisation — including four Regional Heads and the Quality & Compliance Lead — through a period of significant organisational change, building a high-performance culture.

QUALIFICATIONS

- 15–20+ years in facilities management leadership, with significant experience managing a large, complex and geographically diverse FM portfolio within a multinational corporate environment
- Demonstrated track record of leading FM transformation — vendor consolidation, IFM implementation, service standardisation and organisational change at scale
- Direct experience managing global or regional IFM partner relationships at a senior level — contract negotiation, performance management and strategic vendor governance
- Strong financial acumen — experienced in holding direct budget authority for significant FM operational spend
- Exposure to regulated environments — life sciences, Good x Practice (GxP), pharmaceutical or chemical manufacturing — strongly preferred
- Exceptional people leader — able to lead a large, diverse and geographically dispersed organisation through transformation
- Data-driven approach to FM performance — familiar with CAFM/IWMS platforms, KPI frameworks and industry benchmarking standards
- Bachelor's or Master's degree in Facilities Management, Engineering, Business Administration or a related field; IFMA CFM, RICS or equivalent professional qualification advantageous
- Fluency in English required; German advantageous given concentration of portfolio in DACH region

What we offer: We are curious minds that come from a broad range of backgrounds, perspectives, and life experiences. We believe that this variety drives excellence and innovation, strengthening our ability to lead in science and technology. We are committed to creating access and opportunities for all to develop and grow at your own pace. Join us in building a culture of inclusion and belonging that impacts millions and empowers everyone to work their magic and champion human progress!

Apply now and become a part of a team that is dedicated to Sparking Discovery and Elevating Humanity!

jobs.description:

We are the European general agency of the globally active shipping company KAWASAKI KISEN KAISHA Ltd. ("K" Line). As a leading shipping company in the RoRo business, we offer highly sophisti­cated and tailor-made mari­time trans­port solu­tions to our custo­mers from the automotive and heavy machinery indus­tries. As European headquarters based in Hamburg, we are respon­sible for plan­ning and managing the regular services from Europe to North America and Asia as well as their marke­ting in Europe.

Your responsibilities

- Support technical assessment and acceptance of cargoes incl. High & Heavy, special and project cargo as well as review of operational handling
- Support IMDG-related coordination, including documentation review, DG stowage information and operational communication with vessels and ports.
- Participate in cargo quality follow-up, damage prevention, port attendance, vessel feedback and survey-related matters.
- Support QCM/VOS team with analysis of operational deviations, near misses, cargo damage cases and root-cause identification incl. standardization of workflows, SOPs, checklists and digital tools.
- Assist with claims handling by reviewing damage documentation, survey reports, incident reports and operational evidence.
- Prepare and issue voyage instructions, discharging instructions, sailing information and operational updates in internal systems.
- Communicate with vessels, ship management companies, local offices, ports, agents and internal departments to maintain scheduled voyages.
- Support bunkering coordination, including confirmation of fuel specifications and review of bunker supplier information.
- Prepare, review and distribute cargo stowage plans to relevant parties.
- Collect and follow up operational cost reports from local offices.
- Assist with environmental and technical matters related to vessel operations.
- Support operational follow-up in case of disruption, delay, off-hire or other vessel-related incidents.
- Prepare summaries, meeting materials, reports incl. incident reports in case of accidents, serious cargo damage or operational irregularities and coordinate required follow-up actions.

Your profile

- Completed vocational training, university degree or comparable qualification related to shipping, logistics, nautical science, marine operations or port operations.
- Nautical background, sea-going experience, port captain experience or marine technical experience is an advantage.
- Professional experience in RoRo shipping, vessel operations, port logistics, cargo planning, High & Heavy, survey or claims handling is desirable.
- Good understanding of vessel operations, port processes, cargo flow, stowage planning and international communication chains.
- Knowledge of the IMO CSS Code, IMDG Code and SOLAS is an advantage.
- Very good written and spoken English; German language skills are expressly preferred.
- Careful working style, strong affinity for numbers, good prioritization skills and a sense of responsibility in critical situations.
- Willingness to travel to European ports, terminals, vessels and service providers as well as a Class B driving license.

Digital competencies

- Confident use of Microsoft 365, especially Outlook, Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Teams and SharePoint.
- Experience working with structured data, operational reports, Excel analyses and management documents.
- Openness towards digital collaboration tools such as SharePoint Lists, Planner, Loop or comparable solutions.
- Basic understanding and responsible use of modern AI models and AI-supported applications in the daily work context.

We offer:

- Permanent full-time position in an international maritime environment
- Cross-departmental role between Vessel Operations and Quality Control & Marine Technical with a diverse range of responsibilities
- Close collaboration with international colleagues, ports, vessels, OEMs, surveyors, and ship management teams worldwide
- Great intercultural corporate culture with the opportunity to work across global networks
- Attractive remuneration package, including additional benefits such as vacation pay and a 13th monthly salary
- Additional allowances for the Deutschlandticket, fitness center, Ticket Plus® City, and more
- Capital-forming benefits (Vermögenswirksame Leistungen)
- Flexible working hours and attractive mobile working options to support a positive work-life balance
- Modern office conveniently located near a central HVV hub in Hamburg

jobs.occupation: 573787 Business Marketing Manager IGT-Devices (all genders) (Betriebswirt/in (Hochschule) - Marketing)
jobs.description:
To support our initiatives for further adoption of Philips technology providing Class IA guideline treatment options, we are expanding our International marketing team with a Business Marketing Manager DACH, responsible for the full IGTD product and solutions portfolio.

The Business Marketing Manager is the dedicated field-based marketing owner for the DACH market zone, covering Germany, Austria and Switzerland. This role is accountable for translating international and global marketing strategy into locally relevant market activation, demand generation and adoption across the full IGTD product and solutions portfolio. The individual is expected to operate close to the market, spending significant time in the field with sales teams, customers, clinical partners and regional stakeholders to understand local needs, identify growth opportunities and remove barriers to execution.

The role combines strategic portfolio marketing with hands-on field execution. The Business Marketing Manager will define and drive DACH-specific marketing plans, shape customer engagement programs, support priority account activation, build local proof points and ensure launches, campaigns and market development initiatives are executed with strong local relevance and commercial impact.

As a member of the International Marketing team, you will own specific marketing activities that span the complete international region.

Success in this role requires regular travel and visible presence across the zone. The individual should expect to travel extensively within DACH, approximately 50-60% of time, to engage with customers, KOLs, sales teams, professional societies, congresses, workshops and other in-market activation opportunities.

Your role:

Own the DACH market zone

- Act as the primary marketing owner for Germany, Austria and Switzerland, accountable for local market planning, activation priorities and execution quality. Be present in the field with sales team, and customers to understand adoption barriers, customer needs, competetive dynamics and local growth opportunities.
- Collaborate with global and international marketing, market intelligence, and sales leadership to prioritise target accounts, market segments, and growth opportunities across the portfolio.
- Lead specific marketing capabilities internationally, strengthening the broader International marketing organization.
- Translate strategy into local execution by converting global and international portfolio strategies into DACH-specific messaging, campaigns, engagement formats and sales enablement priorities.
- Drive demand generation and adoption by leading marketing activities that increase awareness, utilization and customer preference for the full IGTD portfolio.

Partner internally, externally and represent the voice of the market

- Partner with sales leadership and field teams to prioritize accounts, shape plans, refine messaging and support commercial objectives.
- Bring structured market insights, customer feedback and competitive intelligence back to the international marketing team to influence activation planning and portfolio priorities.
- Seek and develop opportunities to strengthen Philips’ cardiology value proposition for customers in your region by close partnership with adjacent Philips categories such as the One-IGT unique solution offering.
- Build reference sites, customer testimonials, and clinical proof points that resonate with local audiences. Partner with KOLs and professional societies to strengthen Philips’ position in focus markets.
- Work under limited supervision and broad guidelines, serving as the primary marketing contact for assigned portfolio areas and focus markets.
- Define proposals for the mid-term marketing strategy, identifying key market challenges and opportunities early and implementing business plans and goals accordingly.

You're the right fit if:

- Bachelor’s degree in Marketing, Business, Healthcare, or related field.
- 3–5 years of experience in downstream marketing, preferably in healthcare, medtech, or related industries.
- Demonstrated experience managing a broad product and solutions portfolio (not limited to a single category or technology platform).
- Proven ability to lead dedicated market initiatives – owning the full marketing cycle from strategy to execution within specific geographies.
- Strong execution skills with the ability to adapt global strategies for local impact.
- Excellent presentation, communication, and stakeholder management abilities.
- Knowledge of image-guided therapy, interventional systems, or healthcare technology is a plus.
- Must be fluent in German and English languages.
- Willingness to travel 50–60% of time.

Doing meaningful work should come with fair, transparent rewards. The base salary range for this role is € 126,297.80 – € 159,977.21. We determine pay within the range using objective factors, like the skills the role requires, your relevant experience and the responsibility you will have in this role, alongside internal equity and local market considerations.

This role is eligible for Short Term Incentive, with your rewards linked to individual performance and company results. We will share the full approach with you during the interview process, so you can make a clear, informed decision.

Benefits include:

- Annual leave: 30 days
- Mobility and devices: subsidized Germany ticket, leasing opportunities for private use (bicycles, cars, smartphones, ...)
- Philips University & Philips in Balance: wide range of professional training courses for personal development and healthcare
- Philips Pension Fund: employer-funded pension plan
- Philips Partnerzeit: two paid weeks off after your partner has given birth
- Philips MyShop: discount on Philips products
- Culture: informal culture, a paid day for voluntary work, various team and cultural activities, etc.

How we work together
Field roles are most effectively done outside of the company’s main facilities, generally at the customers’ or suppliers’ locations.

About Philips
We are a health technology company. We built our entire company around the belief that every human matters, and we won't stop until everybody everywhere has access to the quality healthcare that we all deserve. Do the work of your life to help the lives of others.

jobs.occupation: Scientific Coordinator (m/f/d) International Max Planck Research School for Ultrafast Imaging & Stru (Projektkoordinator/in (kaufmännisch))
jobs.description:
The Max Planck Society is one of the world’s leading research organizations. Its institutes conduct cutting-edge basic research in the natural sciences, life sciences, social sciences and humanities for the benefit of society. Located in Science City Hamburg Bahrenfeld, the Max Planck Institute for the Structure and Dynamics of Matter (MPSD) investigates the properties and dynamics of matter on the elementary timescales of atomic and electronic motion. Its interdisciplinary research combines experimental and theoretical approaches, with a particular focus on ultrafast phenomena, quantum materials and advanced imaging methods. The International Max Planck Research School for Ultrafast Imaging & Structural Dynamics (IMPRS-UFAST) is a joint initiative of the MPSD, Universität Hamburg, Deutsches Elektronen-Synchrotron (DESY) and European XFEL. It provides outstanding doctoral researchers from around the world with a structured and interdisciplinary training environment at the Hamburg-Bahrenfeld research campus.

To coordinate and further develop this international doctoral program, the MPSD is seeking a highly motivated

Scientific Coordinator (m/f/d) International Max Planck Research School for Ultrafast Imaging & Structural Dynamics (IMPRS-UFAST)

The position offers an excellent opportunity to apply academic experience and transferable skills in a new professional context and to develop a career in science management. We are looking for a candidate who understands the opportunities and challenges of doctoral research from personal experience and is motivated to use this knowledge to support and further develop the next generation of international researchers.

Your position

- Training Programme - Develop and coordinate a semester-based curriculum of scientific courses and transferable-skills training in close collaboration with IMPRS Fellows and Principal Investigators.
- Plan and organize workshops, retreats, networking events and career-development activities tailored to the needs of doctoral researchers.
- Regularly evaluate and further develop the training program to foster interdisciplinary exchange and professional development.
- Annual International Doctoral Recruitment - Coordinate the annual international recruitment and application process, from developing and publishing doctoral projects and launching the call for applications to organizing the selection symposium, conducting interviews and coordinating final admissions.
- Doctoral Mentoring and Career Development - Support doctoral researchers throughout their time in the programme, from admission and onboarding through to completion, serving as a trusted contact for programme-related, administrative and career matters.
- Develop and coordinate initiatives that help doctoral researchers explore and prepare for career opportunities beyond the PhD.
- IMPRS-UFAST Office and Programme Administration - Oversee the day-to-day operations of the IMPRS-UFAST Office and coordinate communication, collaboration and networking among doctoral researchers, academic partners and committees, national and international partner institutions, and the MPSD administration.
- Serve as a member of the IMPRS-UFAST Executive Board and contribute to programme governance by preparing and coordinating meetings, implementing decisions, and overseeing reports, evaluations and programme documentation.
- Coordinate the programme budget and oversee the website, guidelines, application information, records and communication channels, while contributing to quality assurance, alumni relations, academic networking and the strategic development of IMPRS-UFAST.

Your background and skills

- A completed doctorate in the natural sciences; postdoctoral experience is an advantage, but not a requirement.
- A strong understanding of doctoral research, the challenges and opportunities of an academic career, and the German higher-education and research environment.
- A genuine interest in science management and in applying your academic experience and expertise in a broader professional context.
- Strong communication, coordination and project-management skills, demonstrated through experience in research, teaching, mentoring, event organisation or collaborative projects.
- A proactive, independent and structured approach to work, combined with creativity, initiative and a strong ability to work collaboratively.
- Excellent written and spoken English; very good German language skills or a willingness to develop them further are desirable.
- Intercultural sensitivity and the ability to communicate and collaborate effectively with doctoral researchers, senior scientists, administrative colleagues and external partners.

- Previous experience in science management is an advantage, but not a requirement. We particularly welcome candidates with an academic background who are ready to broaden their professional perspective and bring their scientific expertise, international experience and organisational strengths into a new professional context.

Our offer

- A varied and rewarding role at the intersection of science, doctoral education, career development and science management, with scope for initiative, professional growth and the opportunity to contribute your own ideas to the further development of IMPRS-UFAST.
- An international, interdisciplinary and collegial working environment at the Science City Hamburg Bahrenfeld research campus, with a modern workplace and opportunities for collaboration across institutions.
- A wide range of training and professional-development opportunities.
- A family-friendly working environment and active support in balancing work, family and personal life.
- A subsidy for the Profiticket as a Germany ticket.
- Attractive remuneration and social benefits in accordance with the German public pay scale (TVöD Bund), depending on qualifications and professional experience.
- Supplementary pension provision through VBL.
- An initial contract for two years, with the possibility of permanent employment thereafter.

- The Max Planck Society is committed to gender equality, diversity and inclusion. We welcome applications from all backgrounds. The Max Planck Society also aims to increase the number of employees with disabilities and therefore expressly encourages applications from qualified individuals with disabilities.

Your application

Please submit the following documents through our online application portal by 26 October 2026.

- a letter of motivation outlining your interest in science management, doctoral training and the development of IMPRS-UFAST
- your curriculum vitae
- copies of your relevant university degrees and doctoral certificate
- relevant employment certificates or references
- a publication list, if applicable

For questions regarding the position, please contact Dr. Neda Lotfiomran (neda.lotfiomran@mpsd.mpg.de (https://mailto:neda.lotfiomran@mpsd.mpg.de) ) . Detailed information about the Max Planck Institute for the Structure and Dynamics of Matter can be found at http://www.mpsd.mpg.de (http://www.mpsd.mpg.de/) .

We look forward to your application.
